defect_of_record: every pane-side page repaint EVICTS the React-portal ink canvas and nothing ever re-inserts it. Proven three ways: (1) LIVE TRACER on production (4CH1/1C QP viewer, headless Chromium): a MutationObserver on the pane scroller recorded exactly four ink-removed records (pages 1, 3, 4, 2) — each canvas removed from its own still-connected [data-page] holder, ZERO ink-added records — after two Zoom-in clicks; result state inkPerPage=[0,0,0,0,1×24], unrevived by scroll, healed only by reload; the committed mtext visually vanished with its ink subtree (katexLeft 0). (2) CODE PATH: pdf-pane.tsx renderPage (the s145 double-buffer swap, holder.replaceChildren(canvas)) and the off-radius sweep (bare replaceChildren()) are the only writers that empty a holder — correct pdf engineering that evicts the portal-hosted ink canvas as a side effect. (3) THE REACT CONSEQUENCE: a portal whose container children are removed externally stays 'rendered' in React's tree — reconciliation never re-inserts the nodes, and InkLayer's structure-only holder observer reads the batch as 'same holders, no change' (the dedupe keeps prev). Net: after one zoom the re-painted pages' tools are ALL dead (no surface receives pointers) and committed ink visually vanishes until reload
